title: HTTP server with net/http: handlers, mux and the 1.22 routing

videos.script: This course writes one server, and this lesson writes its first lines. {{server}} In Go, a web server is a normal program that never finishes. It waits on a port. Each request goes to a function you wrote. {{handler}} That function has two arguments. One is the request. The other is where your answer goes. {{mux}} Between the port and your functions sits a router, the mux. Since Go 1.22 it understands methods and wildcards. So a GET and a POST on the same path can reach different code, and a 405 is written for you. {{precedence}} When two patterns match, the more specific one wins. When neither is more specific, the program refuses to start, and says why. {{timeouts}} Then the part most tutorials skip. A server built the quick way has no timeouts at all. You will hold a connection open by hand, and watch it stay open. {{boxoffice}} And at the end, boxoffice answers its first requests. It is the service the next sixteen lessons grow.
